title: Why Are Dams Curved?
description:
Some of the tallest dams in the world are thinner than you would believe. A wall of concrete can hold back a lake billions of tonnes heavy, while being only a few meters thick at the top. The secret is the curve. Bend a dam the right way, and the water pushes it tighter against the mountains instead of knocking it over. Today, eleven parts of a dam, and why each one exists.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 11 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:08 1. The curve
2:19 2. The thick wall
3:28 3. The pipes hidden in the concrete
4:40 4. The spillway
5:54 5. The air slots in the tunnel
7:06 6. The towers in the lake
8:11 7. The giant pipes
9:21 8. The tunnels inside the dam
10:27 9. The fish ladder
11:33 10. The mountain that fell into the lake
12:44 11. The dam shared by two countries
13:48 The verdict

Sources:
- Arch, gravity and arch-gravity dams: Wikipedia, "Arch dam" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arch_dam ; Wikipedia, "Gravity dam" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gravity_dam
- Contra (Verzasca) Dam, 220 m, GoldenEye bungee jump: Wikipedia, "Contra Dam" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contra_Dam
- Three Gorges Dam (2,335 m long, 181 m tall, largest power station): Wikipedia, "Three Gorges Dam" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three_Gorges_Dam
- Hoover Dam (660 ft base, cooling pipes ~582 miles, 125-year cooling estimate, four intake towers, two clocks, 30 ft penstocks): US Bureau of Reclamation, "Hoover Dam - Frequently Asked Questions" https://www.usbr.gov/lc/hooverdam/faqs/ ; Wikipedia, "Hoover Dam" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoover_Dam
- Oroville Dam spillway incident (February 2017, ~188,000 evacuated): Independent Forensic Team report (2018) ; Wikipedia, "Oroville Dam crisis" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oroville_Dam_crisis
- Glen Canyon Dam 1983 spillway cavitation, flashboards, aeration slots: US Bureau of Reclamation ; Wikipedia, "Glen Canyon Dam" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glen_Canyon_Dam
- Cavitation: Wikipedia, "Cavitation" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavitation
- Water hammer and surge tanks: Wikipedia, "Water hammer" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_hammer
- Inspection galleries, uplift and drains, plumb lines: US Bureau of Reclamation, "Design of Gravity Dams" ; FEMA dam safety guidelines https://www.fema.gov/emergency-managers/risk-management/dam-safety
- Fish ladders (Bonneville Dam fish counting): US Army Corps of Engineers, Portland District https://www.nwp.usace.army.mil/bonneville/ ; Wikipedia, "Fish ladder" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish_ladder
- Vajont Dam disaster (9 October 1963, ~260 million m3 landslide, ~2,000 deaths, Longarone): Wikipedia, "Vajont Dam" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vajont_Dam
- Itaipu Dam (Brazil-Paraguay 50/50, 20 units at 50 Hz and 60 Hz): Itaipu Binacional https://www.itaipu.gov.br/en ; Wikipedia, "Itaipu Dam" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itaipu_Dam
